items.title: Decreto ministeriale 21 agosto 2026 — Modalità di trasmissione del rapporto sul divario retributivo di genere
items.snippet: Ministero del Lavoro e delle Politiche Sociali. Portale Servizi Lavoro; finestra di trasmissione 2027.
items.headline: Italy fixes the filing channel and window for the pay-gap report: Servizi Lavoro portal, 1 March to 30 June 2027.

summary.text: The report can only be filed through the ministry's Servizi Lavoro portal, using the annexed electronic form.

cite.quote: shall be transmitted exclusively through the Servizi Lavoro portal

summary.text: The first filing window runs from 1 March to 30 June 2027; a report in any other format is treated as not submitted.

cite.quote: The first transmission window opens on 1 March 2027 and closes on 30 June 2027.

obligations.what: file via Servizi Lavoro portal, annexed form only

relevance.why: Procedural, but sets the concrete filing window and the format that counts as compliance.
relevance.action: Diarise the 2027 window; confirm portal credentials for Italian entities.

items.title: Decreto legislativo 5 agosto 2026, n. 118 — Attuazione della direttiva (UE) 2023/970 sulla trasparenza retributiva
items.snippet: Presidenza della Repubblica. Obblighi di rendicontazione dai cento dipendenti; valutazione congiunta delle retribuzioni.
items.headline: Italy transposes the Pay Transparency Directive; annual reporting from 100 employees, first report due 30 June 2027.

summary.text: Employers with at least 100 employees must report their gender pay gap by 30 June each year from 2027.

cite.quote: Employers with at least one hundred employees shall report, by 30 June of each year starting from 2027, the gender pay gap

summary.text: An unjustified gap of 5% or more in any category, not remedied within six months, triggers a mandatory joint pay assessment with worker representatives.

cite.quote: of at least five per cent in any category of workers

summary.text: Applicants gain a right to the pay range before interview, and employers may no longer ask about pay history.

cite.quote: Employers shall not ask applicants about their pay history

relevance.why: First transposition among the scan's jurisdictions; fixes the reporting threshold and first deadline the intent asks about.
relevance.action: Run a pay-gap diagnostic for clients with 100+ employees in Italy before the 2027 reporting window.

items.title: Circolare INL n. 7/2026 — Prime indicazioni operative sugli obblighi di trasparenza retributiva
items.snippet: Ispettorato Nazionale del Lavoro. Calcolo della soglia dimensionale; avvio dell'attività ispettiva.
items.headline: Italian labour inspectorate: headcount is the prior-year average, per legal entity; inspections start only after the first deadline.

summary.text: The 100-employee threshold is the average headcount of the preceding calendar year, with part-time staff counted pro rata.

cite.quote: calculated as the average number of employees in the calendar year preceding the report, counting part-time workers pro rata

summary.text: Group headcount is not aggregated; each entity is tested alone.

cite.quote: the headcount of a corporate group is not aggregated

relevance.why: Answers the threshold-computation question multinational groups with several Italian entities will ask first.
relevance.action: Map Italian entities against the prior-year average headcount rule.

items.title: Avviso di rettifica — Decreto legislativo 5 agosto 2026, n. 118
items.headline: Corrigendum to the Italian transposition decree: 100–149 employee reporters owe a first report in 2027.

summary.text: The three-yearly cycle for employers with 100 to 149 employees now expressly starts with a 2027 report.

cite.quote: the first report being due in 2027

relevance.why: Removes the ambiguity over whether smaller reporters could wait until 2030.
relevance.action: Treat the 2027 deadline as applying to all Italian reporters above 100 employees.

items.title: Comunicato — Tasso di interesse legale per il secondo semestre 2026
items.snippet: Ministero dell'Economia e delle Finanze. Routine.
items.headline: Italy sets the statutory interest rate for H2 2026 — unrelated to pay transparency.

summary.text: The statutory interest rate for the second half of 2026 is 2.0% per annum.

cite.quote: is set at 2.0 per cent per annum

relevance.why: Routine finance-ministry notice with no bearing on the intent.

items.title: Referentenentwurf: Gesetz zur Änderung des Entgelttransparenzgesetzes (Umsetzung der Richtlinie (EU) 2023/970)
items.headline: Germany publishes its draft transposition bill: reporting from 100 employees, fines up to €100,000, consultation to 30 September.

summary.text: The draft extends the individual right to pay information to every employer, dropping the 200-employee floor.

cite.quote: extends the individual right to information to all employers regardless of size

summary.text: Employers with 250 or more employees would report first for calendar 2026; those with 100 or more report annually.

cite.quote: employers with 250 or more employees shall report for the first time in respect of the 2026 calendar year

summary.text: Failure to report would carry a fine of up to €100,000, and the association consultation closes on 30 September 2026.

cite.quote: The consultation period for the associations ends on 30 September 2026.

relevance.why: Germany is the scan's largest jurisdiction and the draft proposes reporting on 2026 data — earlier than the Directive requires.
relevance.action: Clients with 250+ German employees should treat 2026 as a reporting year now; consider a consultation response before 30 September.

items.title: FAQ: Berichtspflichten für Arbeitgeber mit 100 bis 249 Beschäftigten
items.headline: German ministry FAQ: no new obligations for 100–249 employee employers until the amending Act is in force.

summary.text: Until the amending Act takes effect the existing Entgelttransparenzgesetz applies unchanged.

cite.quote: the existing Entgelttransparenzgesetz continues to apply and no new obligations arise

summary.text: Mid-sized employers report every three years, with the Directive's own first deadline of 7 June 2031 unless the bill brings it forward.

cite.quote: the first report is due by 7 June 2031 under the Directive's timetable

relevance.why: Confirms the status quo; useful only as a holding position for mid-sized clients.
relevance.action: Monitor; nothing to do until the bill passes.
